name: manual_52edd9
claim: zsh reserves the bare name 'status' as a read-only special variable (an alias for $?, the last command's exit code) -- assigning to a shell variable literally named 'status' inside a script fails with 'read-only variable: status' and crashes the script (exit 1), even though it works fine in bash. Use a different variable name (e.g. qstatus, job_status) in any script that must run under zsh, which is this session's default shell

decisions.notes: A Monitor poll-loop script (watching a GossipBus task queue for completion) crashed on its first iteration with exactly this error -- caught immediately via the monitor's failure notification and the output-file traceback, fixed by renaming the variable, no functional logic changed. A one-line, easy-to-repeat mistake worth remembering given zsh is this session's default shell (per CLAUDE.md's Shell: zsh) and 'status' is an unusually tempting/common variable name to reach for in coordination-polling scripts specifically.
